title: Ephemeral virtual bucket collapse during failover causing transient unmetered allowance
creator: Maya Chen
summary: During an edge shard failover we observed ephemeral "virtual" per-key buckets collapsing and merging into a single allow path, which produced a short window where some keys received unmetered allowance and caused billing gaps.
description: Problem statement: When a shard failover and route remapping occur concurrently with active credit reservations, the policy engine's ephemeral virtual buckets (used for per-key fast-path accounting) collapse instead of being rehydrated. This results in a temporary union of allowances where multiple keys share a reconstructed bucket and are allowed beyond their configured quotas. Symptoms reported by SRE: a burst of requests from several keys served with no debit events recorded for ~14s, followed by a bulk reconciliation that retroactively marked some tokens but did not map to exact request ids.
reproduction_steps: Provision two edge shards A and B and configure identical per-key windowed quotas for a test org with multiple keys.
Seed steady traffic on keys k1-k6 with 10 qps each and enable credit reservation fast-path for per-key buckets.
Trigger a controlled failover of shard A to shard B (simulate node restart with shard reassign) while a route rebind and metadata refresh are in-flight.
Observe request acceptance and meter logs. Expect per-key debits to continue; actual behavior: some keys accepted without matching debit entries for ~5-20s.
Tail the reconciler and shard reconcile logs to see a bulk correction job that assigns debits to a parent aggregate but not one-to-one to original requests.
Reproduce consistently by adding a small clock jitter (~50ms) to the shard lease renew path during failover in the test harness.
impact_summary: Medium-to-high: Affected customers saw short unmetered windows leading to under-billing and potential quota overuse. Operationally it caused alert storms in the reconciler and transient SLA violations for quota enforcement. Customer-visible impact was limited to specific failover windows but could be triggered by maintenance or region events.
investigation_notes: The ephemeral virtual bucket is an in-memory fast-path structure keyed by (org, route, key) that is reconstructed from the persistent accumulator on shard takeover.

On failover we attempt to 'hydrate' virtual buckets by merging last-known reservations with incoming deltas; the bug occurs when two hydration flows run concurrently and use a noop-merge that drops boundary markers, producing a single collapsed bucket.
Race lives in Hydrator.applyDelta() where it checks presence and then conditionally replaces the in-memory entry without CAS semantics against an inflight reconciler update.
Observed correlation with metadata refresh order: if route alias remap happens before lease ack, the hydrator uses a fallback bucket id which collates unrelated keys.
Reconciler bulk corrections run on a separate window and lack request-id mapping; they use aggregate counters and thus cannot repair per-request billing attribution.
Heap snapshots from a repro show virtual bucket count briefly dropping to ~10% of expected while aggregate counter increases.
Relevant logs: hydrator.trace, shard-lease.debug, reconciler.audit. Timings show a 12-18s window where acceptors allowed requests without debits.
Initial mitigation (hotfix): add conservative short-circuit in acceptor to fall back to strict debit path if hydration is in-progress. Deployed to edge region us-west-2 as rollback.
We surfaced a mitigation flag 'strict-hydrate' to prevent fast-path allowance during reconcile windows; this reduces throughput slightly but avoids underbilling.
Metrics to monitor post-fix: per-key accept-without-debit rate, reconciler-corrections-per-window, virtual-bucket-count, shard-hydration-errors.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed: acceptor now rejects fast-path allow decisions if the hydrator reports 'incomplete' state for that bucket. Temporary feature flag 'avoid-ephemeral-collapse' applied to production edge shards. Ops run reconciliation immediately after failover to limit exposure window. We also increased reconciler frequency for 24h after deployment.
proposed_solution: Primary fix: make Hydrator.applyDelta() use CAS semantics (compare-and-set or versioned ownership token) so two concurrent hydrations cannot replace each other's boundary markers.
Persist boundary markers in the durable accumulator so rehydration can perform idempotent merges instead of blind replaces.
Enhance reconciler to emit per-request attribution metadata during correction, enabling deterministic retroactive accounting where possible.
Add integration test for failover-hydration race that asserts no key experiences accept-without-debit under synthetic failover conditions.
Update monitoring and create alert runbook: alert when accept-without-debit rate > 0.01% over 1m with automated mild throttling and ops page for manual review.
Long-term: replace ephemeral virtual buckets with a versioned LRU structure that survives failover handoff with consensus-based ownership transfer.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests that reliably repro the prior window fail and demonstrate the fix prevents collapse in 1000 randomized failover runs.
No increase in production accept-lack-debit metric after rolling the fix to 3 regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) for 72 hours.
Reconciler corrections still complete within SLO (30s) and do not increase CPU by more than 8% on peacetime traffic.
Feature flag removed once stability validated and after one full month of zero incident recurrences in production.
Documentation updated: design note describing hydration semantics and operator guide for running reconciler and emergency flags.
